ENGLISH — TERMLY EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

4. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a describing word

5. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

6. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goes
   C. going
   D. goed

8. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

9. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.

12. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

13. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

14. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

15. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Pronouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short story and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Listening and Responding: Oral Narratives - Myths and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading: Poem and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes: Simple prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
